correctness.rationale: The five factors are distinct and their conics smooth for characteristic zero or p>=5. Exact integral identities E(F)=7F, U(F)=AF, V(F)=BF, det(E,U,V)=-3F are checked by the embedded standard-library polynomial certificate. Cramer divisibility along every generically smooth irreducible factor proves D(log F)=RE⊕RU⊕RV universally. For p!=7 the syzygies P=7U-AE and Q=7V-BE satisfy P×Q=-21∇F; at p=7 the basis E,W=BU-AV satisfies E×W=-3∇F. Coprimality of gradient follows from Euler when p!=7 and from coprimality of A,B plus generic smoothness when p=7. The cross criterion gives AR degrees (3,3)/(1,5). Hilbert–Burch yields the exact two Hilbert rational functions and eventual dimensions 27/31. Separately computed ranks in degrees 6..11 over F5,F7,F11 agree; these finite checks are not substituted for proof. No assertion about local Tjurina length.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: If one directly reduces the cubic Jacobian basis, its cross coefficient -21 vanishes at seven, so complex freeness does not imply that reduction remains a Jacobian basis. A new integral logarithmic basis is required and yields a distinct degree-(1,5) Jacobian syzygy basis exactly at seven. Thus neither the original paper nor the geometric stabilizer theorem implies the complete claim.

value.rationale: The corrected CL7 is a named degree-seven free conic–line arrangement. An exact universally invertible Saito determinant gives a complete good-characteristic bound p>=5, while at the natural resonance prime 7 the Jacobian syzygies jump from degrees (3,3) to (1,5) and gradient-scheme length from 27 to 31. This structural distinction between logarithmic and Jacobian freeness is not a routine numerical recomputation of the known complex configuration; the prime-range and complete natural Hilbert invariant are motivated by integral reduction.
